details:
I have a suggestion for how the accessory limit should work instead of the current numbered limit system

I feel like a better solution for the limit that wouldn't limit any kind of creativity with the accessories and would keep optimization consistent for all accessories (and would encourage optimization for those who get to make accessories) is a percentage system based on the performance impact of accessories

For example let's say that you have a basic cube that is the bare minimum polygons and has no noticeable impact on performance on its own, that would take up a smaller percentage such as 2% - 5% meaning that maximum amount of cubes would be a high amount that could be used in many ways creatively, and can not go past the 100% limit

Then let's say we have a very high quality accessory that takes up 20% - 30%

This accessory would be slightly more noticeable in its impact, so you would only be able to use a few, or one along with multiple less performance heavy accessories, and would also hit that same performance limit

the performance limit would be a ceiling that isn't so high that it causes issues in certain situations, but wouldn't be too low as to not be limiting with low performance impact accessories

I'm not a game developer so I'm not sure how much of a challenge this would be as something to add, but I feel it would be very effective for optimization while allowing people to be very creative in what they can make using basic shapes with low performance cost

I hope this is seen even if it wouldn't work in reality, but at least hopefully so that something similar could be done with accessories that promotes optimization and allows for creativity in the same way as this idea
title: [1814] accessory limit based on performance concept
